items.name: Team strength persists (Elo + form)
items.statement: A team's prior-game results, Elo-weighted, predict the next game's winner better than prior-season win rates.
items.test: Walk-forward logistic model; log-loss skill vs the prior-season baseline; best-of-K permutation deflation.

deflation.verdict: insufficient permutations for a best-of-K null

items.name: Rest and schedule spot
items.statement: Short weeks, bye edge and rest differential move the result.
items.test: Same walk-forward harness, context feature family, deflation gate.

deflation.verdict: insufficient permutations for a best-of-K null

items.name: Missing starters (verified report) depress the unit
items.statement: The snap-weighted share of a unit's listed starters that the official report marks Out predicts the team's next result, over and above team strength.
items.test: Model with and without out-share features; delta log loss; deflation gate.
items.source: nflverse injuries + depth charts + snap counts

items.name: Backup promotion (2nd/3rd/4th string) matters beyond the injury report
items.statement: Teams starting a backup at a premium position (QB, LT, CB1) underperform their rating.
items.test: Would require tiered features per position; registered here, tested only where the depth chart supplies a tier.
items.result: Depth tiers are published per team and position on the injuries page; no tier feature has been fitted yet because the snapshot has no week column for 2022+.

items.name: Player volume regresses to the player's own recent mean
items.statement: A player's next-game over/under on a fixed line is better predicted by his own prior weeks than by 50/50.
items.test: Laplace-smoothed own-history forecast; log loss vs ln 2; no market price exists so no edge claim.

items.name: Same-team prop overs correlate (game script)
items.statement: Passing yards and receiving yards of teammates move together; receptions and rushing yards compete.
items.test: Measured Pearson r on same-team same-week prop hits, bootstrap CI.

items.name: Cross-game legs are effectively independent
items.statement: Two legs from different games have near-zero correlation, so multiplying marginals is approximately right; same-game legs are not.
items.test: Measured correlation between legs; Gaussian copula joint vs product of marginals.

result.name: 2-leg cross-game parlay (one per season, n=6)

metrics.note: One combination per season; a joint probability is not a payout. With this sample the realised rate is far too noisy to confirm calibration.

G8_market.value: no parlay price, payout or vig in any reachable source

result.claim: Joint probability and realised hit rate only. No payout, no vig, no ROI.

items.name: The model beats the published spread
items.statement: Model win probabilities improve on probabilities implied by the published spread line.
items.test: Reference comparison only, because the line is a single un-timestamped snapshot.
items.result: No timestamped line exists, so the reference comparison cannot establish an edge.

items.name: Division games are less predictable
items.statement: Familiarity compresses margins, so the favourite's advantage shrinks.
items.test: Subgroup log loss and calibration for div_game = 1 vs 0.
items.result: Division flag is inside the context family, which failed to clear deflation.

items.name: Dome/roof and weather effects
items.statement: Domed games have different scoring variance and thus different probability calibration.
items.test: Subgroup calibration by roof; requires minimum subgroup size.
items.result: Registered only; subgroup sizes are too small to gate honestly.
